markets.ai_overview_summary: AI Overview answers with a 20 to 40 guest range; core invitees (wedding party, immediate family both sides, closest friends, close family friends); conventions (shower guests are wedding guests, host confirms list with the bride, separate lists for multiple showers, co-ed formats). Cites The Knot, Zola, Emily Post, Elegant Wedding, GigSalad, WeddingWire, Reddit, TikTok.

cross_market_insights: The organic SERP is weak in every market: forum threads, a Facebook group post, Pinterest, a 2012 magazine column and an old hobby checklist hold the top 3. Only one editorial page (bridesdiary.com.au, an Australian directory) makes a top 3. A structured, current editorial guide can rank quickly, consistent with the KD 2 in Zoho.

Google answers the head question in an AI Overview built from US sources (The Knot, Zola, Emily Post). To earn the citation and the click we need a crisp answer block up top (who, how many, who decides) plus depth the AI Overview lacks.

No top result covers the destination wedding case: a small guest list abroad, people who cannot travel, shower at home vs near the wedding, or joining by video. A Reddit r/DestinationWeddings thread ranking in Melbourne shows real demand for exactly this.
Australian vocabulary is missing from the US-led answers: kitchen tea, hens. AU searchers see US wording ('maid of honor', 'wedding shower').

Most sources state etiquette as fixed rules. Our angle frames it as convention and advice with the reasons behind it, which reads better to our 30s AU couple and avoids contradicting real family dynamics.
Searchers want a usable list: image pack is printable guest list sheets (Etsy, template sites) and an Instagram checklist post ranks. A printable checklist is a direct gap for editorial sites.

US demand is far higher on 'who to invite to bridal shower' (1,600) and 'bridal shower etiquette' (720) than the primary keyword (140). AU volumes are tiny (10 to 30). Traffic will be mostly US unless the AU angle is clear; the piece should serve both without US spelling.
payload.recommended_angle: The calm, current guide to who goes on a bridal shower (kitchen tea) guest list, framed as convention not rules: who usually gets invited and why, who decides, how big, the awkward middle (in-laws, work friends, partners), and the case no one covers, a destination wedding with a small guest list abroad, guests who cannot travel and virtual guests. Ends with a printable checklist that also works inside Wonderland Studio.
